etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English alien, a borrowing from Old French alien, aliene, from Latin aliēnus (“belonging to someone else”, later “exotic, foreign”), from Latin alius (“other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos. Related to English else.

definitions.definition: A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.

quote.citation: 2023 March 21 (last accessed), NOBANIS: European Network on Invasive Species‎[1]:
quote.text: An animated film intended to inform travellers about the dangers that alien species present to Arctic ecosystems is being released today. The message is that it is important to ensure that nobody accidentally brings alien species with them as stowaways in their clothing, baggage or equipment.

definitions.definition: (sometimes derogatory) A person in a country not their own.

quote.citation: 1773, William Blackstone, Commentaries on the laws of England: in four books, 5th edition, volume 1, page 372:
quote.text: An alien born may purchase lands, or other estates: but not for his own use; for the king is thereupon entitled to them.

quote.citation: 1831, John Marshall, Cherokee Nation v. Georgia, U.S. Government:
quote.text: The counsel have shown conclusively that they are not a state of the union, and have insisted that individually they are aliens, not owing allegiance to the United States.

quote.citation: 1987, “Englishman in New York”, in …Nothing Like the Sun, performed by Sting:
quote.text: I'm an alien, I'm a legal alien  I'm an Englishman in New York

quote.citation: 2004, Wesley Campbell, Stephen Court, Be a hero: the battle for mercy and social justice, Destiny Image Publishers, page 74:
quote.text: Aliens are aliens because of persecution or war or hardship or famine.

definitions.definition: Any life form of extraterrestrial or extradimensional origin.

quote.citation: 2010, BioWare, Mass Effect 2, Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →OCLC, PC, scene: Hello from the Reds:
quote.text: You might not have much use for me. You spend too much time with the damn aliens, pretending your time in the gangs back on Earth never happened. I know you weren't happy when I found you at the Citadel a couple years back.But I'm glad you're on this. I hope you find whoever took my people on Freedom's Progress and kick their scaly asses. I'm glad it's a human finding these bastards.

definitions.definition: One excluded from certain privileges; one alienated or estranged.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Ephesians 2:12, column 2:
quote.text: […] aliens from the common wealth of Iſrael […]

quote.citation: 1928, Philip Mauro, “The Character of the Sermon on the Mount”, in The Gospel of the Kingdom, with an Examination of Modern Dispensationalism‎[2] (Religion), Boston: Hamilton Brothers, →OCLC, page 182:
quote.text: The One Who, in this marvellous utterance, brings those who were by nature aliens and enemies of God into intimate and holy relations with God the Father, is the very One Who had to come to offer that Sacrifice without which such relationship would have been forever an impossibility; without which there would have been nothing for the best of men but death and judgment and the lake of fire.

definitions.definition: Not belonging to the same country, land, or government, or to the citizens or subjects thereof; foreign.
Pertaining to extraterrestrial life; typical of an extraterrestrial creature.

quote.citation: 1982, Douglas Adams, Life, the Universe and Everything, page 8:
quote.text: It had a peculiar alien tallness, a peculiar alien flattened head, peculiar slitty little alien eyes[.]

definitions.definition: (law) To transfer the ownership of something.
